description: The Gmail accounts connected to Pheeme.
name: list_accounts
title: List accounts

description: Each account's labels (system and user) with their conversation counts.

account.description: Email address (or id) of one connected account. Leave out for all accounts.

name: list_labels
title: List labels

description: Conversations in a mailbox, newest first: inbox, primary, social, promotions, updates, forums, starred, important, sent, drafts, spam, trash, all (everything outside Spam and Trash), or a user label's name. Answered from Pheeme's local copy, so it's instant. To count or rank (how many, who sends the most), use count_mail instead of paging through.

account.description: Email address (or id) of one connected account. Leave out for all accounts.

compact.description: Leave out snippets and labels (default false).

cursor.description: The cursor from the previous page, to get the next one.

name: list_mailbox
title: List a mailbox

description: Search with Gmail syntax (from:, to:, subject:, label:, is:unread, has:attachment, newer_than:7d, in:trash...). Searches the mail cached on this computer by default, which is instant but may not hold old mail; set gmail to true to ask Gmail's own search, which covers the whole mailbox. Queries only Gmail understands go to Gmail automatically. Like Gmail, it leaves out Trash and Spam unless the query says in:anywhere, in:trash or in:spam.

account.description: Email address (or id) of one connected account. Leave out for all accounts.

compact.description: Leave out snippets and labels (default false).

cursor.description: The cursor from the previous page, to get the next one.

name: search_mail
title: Search mail

description: How many conversations a mailbox or a search holds, and how many are unread, optionally grouped by sender, domain (the sender's), label, tab (inbox tab) or month, biggest group first. One call answers questions like "who has the most unread mail in Promotions" (mailbox: promotions, unread_only: true, group_by: sender) without listing the mail. Counts the mail on this computer (search_mail's local syntax).

account.description: Email address (or id) of one connected account. Leave out for all accounts.

mailbox.description: A mailbox, as list_mailbox takes it (default inbox).

query.description: A search, as search_mail takes it. Instead of mailbox.

name: count_mail
title: Count mail

description: A conversation's messages as plain text, with senders, recipients, dates, labels and attachment names. Bodies not cached yet are downloaded from Gmail.

account.description: The account the conversation is in (from the list or search result).

name: get_thread
title: Read a conversation

description: Every Gmail filter (rule) on the account: what it matches and what it does, in words, with flags for filters that delete mail, skip the inbox or mark it read.

account.description: Email address (or id) of one connected account. Leave out for all accounts.

name: list_filters
title: List Gmail filters

description: The senders with the most mail over the last N days (default 90), from Pheeme's local copy: how many messages, how many are unread or sit in Inbox, Trash or Spam, which inbox tab they land in, how often the user has written to them (you_wrote; none suggests a list or notification, not a person), and whether their mail offers unsubscribe (one_click, link, email, none, or unknown). Counts that are 0 are left out. Use it to suggest filters or unsubscribing; for plain counts, count_mail is lighter.

account.description: Email address (or id) of one connected account. Leave out for all accounts.

tab.description: Only mail in this inbox tab.

name: sender_report
title: Who sends the most mail

description: For each Gmail filter that deletes, archives or marks mail read (or every filter with all: true), the mail it matched over the last N days (default 30), found with Gmail's search: how much (matched, first 50), where it is now (now_in: trash, inbox, archived...) and a sample. For filters that delete, archive or mark read, worth_checking lists matched mail from the last year that looks wanted (starred, in Primary or Updates, or an order, bill, delivery or account subject); read it before trusting the filter. Use it to find filters that catch mail the user wants; fix them with delete_filter and create_filter, and rescue what they trashed or archived with move_to_inbox.

account.description: Email address (or id) of one connected account. Leave out for all accounts.

compact.description: Leave out snippets and labels (default false).

name: filter_audit
title: What filters caught

title: Create a label

description: Create a Gmail filter (rule) for mail that arrives from now on. Give at least one criterion (from, to, subject, query, negated_query, has_attachment) and one action. Before creating one that trashes or archives mail, check what it would catch with search_mail (gmail: true) using the same criteria.

account.description: The account (email address or id). Required when more than one is connected.

add_label.description: A user label's name (it must exist).

category.description: File it under an inbox tab.

from.description: Sender address, domain or Gmail from: value.

description: Unsubscribe from the mailing list a conversation came from, using its List-Unsubscribe header. One-click unsubscribes (RFC 8058) happen at once; otherwise the answer gives the link or address for the user to use themselves. Uses the newest message not sent by the user, or message_id.

account.description: The account (email address or id). Required when more than one is connected.

name: unsubscribe

description: Save a draft in Gmail Drafts for the user to review and send from Pheeme. Assistants can't send mail. For a reply, give reply_to_message_id (a message_id from get_thread): recipients, subject and the quoted original come from it, and to/cc/bcc add more. Pheeme adds the user's signature (as set in Settings › Compose), so don't sign the body.

account.description: The account (email address or id). Required when more than one is connected.

name: create_draft

name: list_calendars
title: List calendars

description: Events between from and to (default the next 7 days from the start of today), repeating events expanded, from Pheeme's local copy of the calendars the user shows. With query, only events whose title, place, description or guests contain every word. Times are in the user's Calendar time zone unless time_zone says otherwise.

account.description: Email address (or id) of one connected account. Leave out for all accounts.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone (Europe/Paris) for reading and writing times. Default: the user's Google Calendar time zone.

to.description: A date (that whole day counts) or date-time.

name: list_events
title: List events

account.description: The account (email address or id). Required when more than one is connected.

calendar_id.description: calendar_id from list_events (default the primary calendar).

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone (Europe/Paris) for reading and writing times. Default: the user's Google Calendar time zone.

name: get_event
title: Read an event

description: Free slots of at least duration_minutes (default 30) between from and to (default now to 7 days on), inside working hours (day_start to day_end, default 09:00 to 17:00, weekdays unless weekends is true). Busy means a timed event the user hasn't declined and that isn't marked free, on any shown calendar of the accounts (all, or account); all-day events don't count.

account.description: Email address (or id) of one connected account. Leave out for all accounts.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone (Europe/Paris) for reading and writing times. Default: the user's Google Calendar time zone.

to.description: A date (that whole day counts) or date-time.

name: find_free_time

end.description: A date-time (2026-11-20T15:00, read in time_zone, or with an offset) or, for an all-day event, a date (2026-11-20).

notify_guests.description: Email the guests about it (default false: the event changes on their calendars without an email). Ask the user before setting it.

start.description: A date-time (2026-11-20T15:00, read in time_zone, or with an offset) or, for an all-day event, a date (2026-11-20).

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone (Europe/Paris) for reading and writing times. Default: the user's Google Calendar time zone.
